A1.justification: Both PDFs describe KVFundaBench and ShotKV. Their main text, figures, tables, equations and complete appendices are readable and support comparison despite the changed title and organization.

before.justification: v2 reports original benchmark evaluations, attention and compression-sensitivity analyses, ShotKV accuracy results, and latency measurements in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v3 retains these empirical results and adds document-QA evaluation, component ablations, prompt-robustness tests and Qwen3 results.

M1.justification: v3 Section 5.1 and Algorithm 1 replace scores summed across layers with independent per-layer scoring and retention in both phases. It also adapts ShotKV to sentences as semantic units for HotpotQA. These revise the retained two-phase framework, although Appendix F.1 still contains conflicting cross-layer scoring prose.

E1.justification: The original fundamental-capability and long-context tasks are retained. HotpotQA adds multi-hop document QA without few-shot exemplars, extending the evaluated task requirements beyond the existing coverage (v3 Tables 3 and 18).

E2.justification: v3 adds Random Shot to the many-shot comparison, Prefill-only comparisons against ShotKV, and ChunkKV and SnapKV to the efficiency comparison previously limited to FullKV and ShotKV. The existing accuracy experiments retain their original compression baselines.

E3.justification: v3 substantially extends the evaluation design with phase-removal and prompt-perturbation controls, Qwen3-4B-Base settings, and a matched model/method/ratio comparison reporting absolute performance drops. Original shot counts, temperature and LG-GSM8K parameters are retained. However, Table 11's claimed many-shot and compression-ratio settings conflict with retained GSM8K tables.

E4.justification: v3 newly tests attention-based selection against Random Shot, removes decoding compression on LG-GSM8K and many-shot GSM8K, and shuffles or replaces exemplars (Tables 4 and 12–14). These substantially expand evidence about ShotKV's components and prompt robustness beyond v2's task, model and shot-count analyses.

E5.justification: The existing confidence-interval plots are retained. v3 adds no seed or repeated-run disclosures, uncertainty estimates or statistical tests. Its numbered reorderings and exemplar replacements are separate experimental conditions, not reported repeated-run uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: Appendix Tables 6–10, the main ShotKV accuracy values and its latency measurements are retained. v3 substantially adds HotpotQA, Qwen3, ablation, robustness and comparator-efficiency results. For example, new HotpotQA results at 10% retention report ShotKV at 43.60 versus PyramidKV at 43.80. These are additional findings, not demonstrated version-to-version performance gains.

T1.justification: Equation 5 replaces v2's exact score-maximizing subset formulation and optimality language with budget-constrained TopK selection, closer to the stated greedy procedure. Equations 3 and 7 also redefine scores per layer. These are limited mathematical revisions; no theorems or proofs are added.

C1.justification: v3 explicitly recasts ShotKV from a novel compression framework into a proof of concept without an algorithmic-novelty claim, foregrounding high-density reasoning versus retrieval. The abstract and contributions add document-QA generalization and latency claims, although the latency evidence already appeared in v2 Appendix C.2.

C2.justification: v2's brief limitations become substantive qualifications about KV-cache access, heuristic scoring, recoverable semantic units and unresolved unstructured zero-shot settings. v3 also adds hypotheses about reinforcement-learning-derived reasoning robustness and safety-critical prompt fragmentation, and interprets efficiency as comparable to existing compressors.

D1.justification: v3 Appendix A newly supplies a repository location and states that ShotKV, evaluation scripts and configuration files are released. It also names KVpress alongside the existing evaluation harness. Previously disclosed temperature, shot counts, A40 hardware and batch-size information are retained.

R1.justification: v3 substantially revises ShotKV's positioning relative to ChunkKV's semantic chunks and SCOPE's phase separation, explicitly narrowing novelty. It also expands coverage of recent research, including Expected Attention, KVzip, FlowKV, OracleKV, SONIC and KV quantization; publication-metadata updates alone are not counted.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction and ShotKV motivation are substantially rewritten around semantic integrity. v3 adds main-text related-work and limitations sections and reorganizes the appendices around code availability, extended discussion and additional experiments.

P2.justification: v3 changes the main text to two columns and extensively resizes and relocates the retained figures, including vertically arranging Figure 3's panels. It reformats comparison tables, moves expanded efficiency results into the main text, and adds QA, ablation and robustness displays.

improvement.justification: New component and prompt-robustness controls, document-QA evidence, and clearer novelty and applicability limits improve on v2's support for ShotKV. The gain is constrained by introduced inconsistencies: Table 11's many-shot baseline and 30% scores conflict with retained GSM8K tables, while Appendix F.1 contradicts the updated per-layer algorithm. These weaken validation and reproducibility, limiting the overall improvement.
